title: Linux 7.3-rc2 Released Following Another Busy Week
summary: Linux 7.3-rc2 release candidate marks progress toward stable v7.3 kernel with active development cycle ongoing. For 5G RAN embedded developers, this release cycle introduces potential driver updates, networking stack improvements, and real-time performance enhancements critical for DU/CU workload optimization. Key focus: early testing of rc2 is essential to identify stability issues before production deployment in communication infrastructure.

title: [$] Fixing the TCMalloc regression with RSEQ operations
summary: This article addresses a kernel regression in restartable sequences (RSEQ) that broke TCMalloc memory allocator in Linux 6.19, where user-space lockless operations relied on undocumented kernel behavior. For embedded/5G firmware developers, this highlights critical compatibility issues between kernel optimization changes and memory management in real-time systems, requiring careful validation of RSEQ-dependent code in high-performance RAN applications.
raw_snippet:
The restartable sequences feature is one of
the stranger corners of the kernel's user-space interface; it provides a
way for user space to carry out simple lockless operations and be informed
if it is preempted over the course of an operation (and must, thus,
restart). Work merged in the 6.19 release to improve the performance of restartable
sequences broke the TCMalloc allocator ,
which was relying on an undocumented (and unintended) kernel behavior.

title: YuzukiNeko – A Linux-capable Allwinner F101 RISC-V SBC with Raspberry Pi Pico form factor
summary: YuzukiNeko introduces a Pico-sized RISC-V SBC featuring Allwinner's F101 SoC with C907 core, MIPI DSI/LVDS display support, and GPIO headers for Linux deployment. title: MonoMoE: An Efficient Fused Mega-kernel for Quantized MoE Decoding
summary: MonoMoE is proposed as an efficient fused mega-kernel designed to optimize quantized Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoding. It addresses computation inefficiencies in sparse expert execution by eliminating token-major tiling overheads.

title: Waves on the Walls: Empirical Characterization of mmWave Lateral Waves for Enhanced Indoor Coverage
summary: This work empirically characterizes lateral wave propagation along building interfaces for mmWave coverage extension, introducing a paradigm shift from traditional obstacle-avoidance beamforming strategies. For 5G RAN firmware developers, this provides novel channel modeling insights essential for optimizing indoor mmWave beamforming algorithms, antenna array tuning, and coverage enhancement in FR2 bands without relying on conventional line-of-sight propagation assumptions.

title: Why faster coding isn't making delivery any faster
summary: While generative AI significantly accelerates individual code writing, it does not necessarily translate to faster software delivery cycles. The bottleneck often shifts to code integration, testing, and verifying the overall quality of AI-generated code.
raw_snippet: Generative AI promised to eliminate one of the biggest sources of friction in software engineering: Writing code. In many ways, it has delivered. Today, an AI coding agent can implement features in minutes that might have taken an engineer an hour. It can generate tests, refactor code, write documentation, navigate large repositories, and even execute development tasks autonomously. summary: The systemd 262-rc2 release introduces an AI canary designed to detect unreviewed AI/LLM-generated code submissions in pull requests. The release also includes standard bug fixes and optimizations for the init system and service manager.
raw_snippet: One week after releasing systemd 262-rc1, systemd 262-rc2 is now available with further fixes and refinements for this init system and service manager. title: The context wall: What happens when your AI agent hits the GPU memory ceiling
summary: This article explains the constraints of GPU memory when handling large context windows in AI models during production. Exceeding these physical memory limits results in silent failures as the hardware hits its capacity ceiling.
raw_snippet: Every model has a physical limit to how much it can hold in active memory at once. When production workloads hit that limit, they hit the context wall, and the failure is silent.An AI model's context window is the amount of text it can hold and reason over at a given time. Every token in the window has to be held in graphics processing unit (GPU) memory the model can actively attend to. title: NVIDIA BlueField security and acceleration arrive on the Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA and Red Hat OpenShift
summary: NVIDIA BlueField DPU offloads packet routing and security policies from host CPUs, reducing infrastructure tax from 30% CPU overhead; critical for 5G RAN and core network functions where eliminating CPU cycles spent on networking allows dedicated resources for radio access network processing and AI inference workloads.
raw_snippet: Agentic AI inference and 5G RAN workloads are pushing data center networking to its limits, yet up to 30% of host CPU power is wasted simply routing packets and enforcing security policies.
